jesus.name: Jesus
jesus.note: The Lord; calm authority, tender with the afflicted, grave in discourse.

the-jews.name: The Jews
the-jews.note: The Judean authorities and their party; hostile, pressing, sometimes merely onlookers.

other-jews.name: Others of the Jews
other-jews.note: A second party among the Jews answering or doubting the first.

disciples.name: Disciples
disciples.note: The Twelve; questioning, anxious for their master.

thomas.name: Thomas
thomas.note: Thomas called Didymus; grim, loyal resolve.

martha.name: Martha
martha.note: Sister of Lazarus; grieving but full of faith, practical.

mary-of-bethany.name: Mary of Bethany
mary-of-bethany.note: Sister of Lazarus; weeping at the feet of Jesus.

sisters-of-lazarus.name: Martha and Mary
sisters-of-lazarus.note: The sisters of Lazarus sending word to Jesus; urgent, trusting.

council-members.name: Council members
council-members.note: Chief priests and Pharisees in council; alarmed, calculating.

high-priest.name: Caiphas
high-priest.note: High priest that year; curt, contemptuous, politic.

crowd.name: Crowd
crowd.note: The multitude of pilgrims and hearers; acclaiming, wondering, questioning.

1.t: Now there was a certain man sick, named Lazarus, of Bethania, of the town of Mary and of Martha her sister.

2.t: (And Mary was she that anointed the Lord with ointment and wiped his feet with her hair: whose brother Lazarus was sick.)

3.t: His sisters therefore sent to him, saying:
Lord, behold, he whom thou lovest is sick.
3.q: message sent by both sisters (through a messenger); given to the sisters as a pair

4.t: And Jesus hearing it, said to them:
This sickness is not unto death, but for the glory of God: that the Son of God may be glorified by it.

5.t: Now Jesus loved Martha and her sister Mary and Lazarus.

6.t: When he had heard therefore that he was sick, he still remained in the same place two days.

7.t: Then after that, he said to his disciples:
Let us go into Judea again.

8.t: Rabbi, the Jews but now sought to stone thee. And goest thou thither again?

9.t: Are there not twelve hours of the day? If a man walk in the day he stumbleth not, because he seeth the light of this world:

10.t: But if he walk in the night, he stumbleth, because the light is not in him.

11.t: These things he said; and after that he said to them:
Lazarus our friend sleepeth: but I go that I may awake him out of sleep.

12.t: Lord, if he sleep, he shall do well.

13.t: But Jesus spoke of his death: and they thought that he spoke of the repose of sleep.

14.t: Then therefore Jesus said to them plainly:

15.t: And I am glad, for your sakes; that I was not there, that you may believe. But, let us go to him.

16.t: Thomas therefore, who is called Didymus, said to his fellow disciples:
Let us also go, that we may die with him.

17.t: Jesus therefore came: and found that he had been four days already in the grave.

18.t: (Now Bethania was near Jerusalem, about fifteen furlongs off.)

19.t: And many of the Jews were come to Martha and Mary, to comfort them concerning their brother.

20.t: Martha therefore, as soon as she heard that Jesus was come, went to meet him: but Mary sat at home.

21.t: Lord, if thou hadst been here, my brother had not died.

22.t: But now also I know that whatsoever thou wilt ask of God, God will give it thee.

24.t: I know that he shall rise again, in the resurrection at the last day.

25.t: I am the resurrection and the life: he that believeth in me, although he be dead, shall live:

26.t: And every one that liveth and believeth in me shall not die for ever. Believest thou this?

27.t: Yea, Lord, I have believed that thou art Christ, the Son of the living God, who art come into this world.

28.t: And when she had said these things, she went and called her sister Mary secretly, saying:
The master is come and calleth for thee.

29.t: She, as soon as she heard this, riseth quickly and cometh to him.

30.t: For Jesus was not yet come into the town: but he was still in that place where Martha had met him.

31.t: The Jews therefore, who were with her in the house and comforted her, when they saw Mary, that she rose up speedily and went out, followed her, saying:
She goeth to the grave to weep there.

32.t: When Mary therefore was come where Jesus was, seeing him, she fell down at his feet and saith to him.
Lord, if thou hadst been here, my brother had not died.

33.t: Jesus, therefore, when he saw her weeping, and the Jews that were come with her weeping, groaned in the spirit and troubled himself,

34.q: "they" are Mary and the Jews with her (v33); given to the group

37.t: Could not he that opened the eyes of the man born blind have caused that this man should not die?
37.q: "some of them", the sceptical part of the mourners; second group voice

38.t: Jesus therefore again groaning in himself, cometh to the sepulchre. Now it was a cave; and a stone was laid over it.

39.t: Martha, the sister of him that was dead, saith to him:
Lord, by this time he stinketh, for he is now of four days.

40.t: Did not I say to thee that if thou believe, thou shalt see the glory of God?

41.t: They took therefore the stone away. And Jesus lifting up his eyes, said:
Father, I give thee thanks that thou hast heard me.

42.t: And I knew that thou hearest me always: but because of the people who stand about have I said it, that they may believe that thou hast sent me.

43.t: When he had said these things, he cried with a loud voice:

44.t: And presently he that had been dead came forth, bound feet and hands with winding bands. And his face was bound about with a napkin. Jesus said to them:
Loose him and let him go.

45.t: Many therefore of the Jews, who were come to Mary and Martha and had seen the things that Jesus did, believed in him.

46.t: But some of them went to the Pharisees and told them the things that Jesus had done.

47.t: The chief priests, therefore, and the Pharisees gathered a council and said:
What do we, for this man doth many miracles?

48.t: If we let him alone so, all will believe in him; and the Romans will come, and take away our place and nation.

49.t: But one of them, named Caiphas, being the high priest that year, said to them:

50.t: Neither do you consider that it is expedient for you that one man should die for the people and that the whole nation perish not.

51.t: And this he spoke not of himself: but being the high priest of that year, he prophesied that Jesus should die for the nation.

52.t: And not only for the nation, but to gather together in one the children of God that were dispersed.

53.t: From that day therefore they devised to put him to death.

54.t: Wherefore Jesus walked no more openly among the Jews: but he went into a country near the desert, unto a city that is called Ephrem. And there he abode with his disciples.

55.t: And the pasch of the Jews was at hand: and many from the country went up to Jerusalem, before the pasch, to purify themselves.

56.t: They sought therefore for Jesus; and they discoursed one with another, standing in the temple:
What think you that he is not come to the festival day?

57.t: And the chief priests and Pharisees had given a commandment that, if any man knew where he was, he should tell, that they might apprehend him.
